ImageDescription.value:
Refrigerator with some poorly stored and placed items for food safety and contributes to food waste, on June 8, 2020, in San Antonio, TX.

The refrigerator shows recommended and unrecommended storage practices. It is always recommended to keep your refrigerator and pantry clean and organized so you can see what needs to be eaten first. If fresh food is âout of sight, out of mindâ, it may be forgotten and ultimately wasted. Food is less likely to go bad when you use the more perishable and older items first. Also, storing food in clear containers can help you see what you have available in your fridge and pantry and can help you avoid buying food you already have. In the fridge, extend the life of your food by putting it in the right place. For example, the temperature in the refrigerator door fluctuates more than the cabinets or the back of the unit so donât store perishable foods like milk and eggs in the door. Transfer uneaten food from single use containers into sealable containers or wrapped securely.

For more FSIS Food Safety refrigerator tips please see - fsis.usda.gov/wps/portal/fsis/topics/food-safety-education/get-answers/food-safety-fact-sheets/safe-food-handling/refrigeration-and-food-safety/ct_index
